notes.heading: Match the verb and locate the postposition
paragraphs: Simple Hindi statements often place the verb at the end, but agreement and postpositions carry relationships that word order alone cannot express. A habitual statement with a masculine singular subject commonly uses -ता है, while a feminine singular subject commonly uses -ती है. A masculine plural subject commonly uses -ते हैं. A noun before a postposition may take an oblique form: लड़का becomes लड़के before के पास. Possession expressed with के पास is a useful separate pattern; do not translate every English 'have' construction by inserting a verb in the English position.

questions.prompt: Translate 'The boys read every day' using लड़के, रोज़ and पढ़ना. Explain the habitual verb and copula.
solution: Use masculine plural पढ़ते to agree with लड़के.
Use हैं for the plural subject.
markingPoints: Use हैं and explain plural agreement.

questions.prompt: Translate 'The boy has a book' using लड़का, के पास and किताब. Explain why लड़का changes form.
questions.answer: लड़के के पास एक किताब है। The postposition phrase requires the oblique लड़के.
solution: Use के पास to express possession in this sentence.
Change masculine singular लड़का to its oblique form before the postposition.

questions.prompt: Correct 'रीना रोज़ पढ़ता हैं' as a simple habitual statement about one girl named Reena, and name both repairs.
solution: Use feminine singular पढ़ती for Reena.
Use singular है rather than plural हैं in this specified non-honorific sentence.
